'''Anfernee Tyrik Simons''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|n|f|ər|n|i}} {{respell|AN|fər|nee}};<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517083503/https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |url-status=live }}</ref> born June 8, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After high school, he played basketball during a [[postgraduate year]] at the [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]], before being selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the first round of the [[2018 NBA draft]] with the 24th overall pick. Simons was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in 2025 and to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2026.

==Early life==

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2025)===
Simons was selected 24th overall by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Holdahl |first=Casey |date=June 21, 2018 |title=Trail Blazers Select Anfernee Simons in First Round of NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-select-anfernee-simons-first-round-nba-draft |access-date=May 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=June 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610230456/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-select-anfernee-simons-first-round-nba-draft |url-status=live }}</ref> He would be the [[List of NBA high school draftees|third high school player]] since 2015 to be drafted in the NBA, behind [[Thon Maker]] and [[Satnam Singh Bhamara]]. On July 2, 2018, the Trail Blazers announced that they had signed Simons.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gauruder |first=Dana |date=July 2, 2018 |title=Trail Blazers Sign First-Rounder Anfernee Simons |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/07/trail-blazers-sign-first-rounder-anfernee-simons.html |access-date=May 4, 2023 |website=hoopsrumors.com |archive-date=May 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505005037/https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/07/trail-blazers-sign-first-rounder-anfernee-simons.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 21, 2019, the Blazers assigned Simons to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] for an [[NBA G League]] assignment.<ref>{{cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers Assign Anfernee Simons and Gary Trent Jr to G-League |url=https://ripcityproject.com/2019/01/20/portland-trail-blazers-assign-anfernee-simons-gary-trent-jr-g-league/ |work=[[FanSided]] |date=January 20, 2019 |access-date=January 27, 2019 |archive-date=January 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130121231/https://ripcityproject.com/2019/01/20/portland-trail-blazers-assign-anfernee-simons-gary-trent-jr-g-league/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 10, 2019, Simons had his first career start against the Sacramento Kings while the Trail Blazers rested [[Damian Lillard]] and [[CJ McCollum]] for the final game of the regular season. Simons put up career highs across the board with 37 points, six rebounds, and nine assists, becoming the first Trail Blazers rookie to score 30-plus points since Lillard.

In the championship round of the [[Slam Dunk Contest]] during halftime of the [[2021 NBA All-Star Game]], Simons attempted to kiss the rim, but failed and still completed the dunk. Despite his failed attempt, Simons was named the 2021 Slam Dunk Champion on a 3–2 decision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-att-slam-dunk|title=Trail Blazers' Anfernee Simons wins 2021 AT&T Slam Dunk|website=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=March 17, 2021|archive-date=February 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210223044059/https://www.nba.com/news/2021-att-slam-dunk|url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 3, 2022, Simons scored a then career-high 43 points behind nine three-pointers, along with seven assists, in a 136–131 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. In a postgame interview, he dedicated the game to his grandfather who died of cancer the previous night.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/anfernee-simons-helps-blazers-overcome-trae-youngs-56-points-with-43-point-outburst-after-grandfathers-death/|title= Anfernee Simons helps Blazers overcome Trae Young's 56 points with 43-point outburst after grandfather's death|access-date= January 4, 2022|archive-date= January 4, 2022|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220104070238/https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/anfernee-simons-helps-blazers-overcome-trae-youngs-56-points-with-43-point-outburst-after-grandfathers-death/|url-status= live}}</ref> On March 28, Simons was ruled out for the remainder of the season with [[patellar tendinopathy]] in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS INJURY UPDATES |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-injury-updates |access-date=March 28, 2022 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=September 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920163856/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-injury-updates |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 25, 2023, Simons suffered a torn UCL in his right thumb against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], ruling him out for four to six weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers' Anfernee Simons needs thumb surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38758242/trail-blazers-anfernee-simons-needs-thumb-surgery |access-date=October 28, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=October 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231027222703/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38758242/trail-blazers-anfernee-simons-needs-thumb-surgery |url-status=live }}</ref>

On December 19, 2024, Simons had a double-double and hit the game-winning buzzer-beater against the [[2024–25 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhatia |first=Swati |date=2024-12-20 |title=NBA Top 10: Anfernee Simons' game winning buzzer-beater steals the show |url=https://theplayoffs.news/en/nba-top-10-anfernee-simons-game-winning-buzzer-beater-steals-the-show/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |work=The Playoffs |archive-date=December 20, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241220094807/https://theplayoffs.news/en/nba-top-10-anfernee-simons-game-winning-buzzer-beater-steals-the-show/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Simons started 70 games for Portland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 19.3 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 4.8 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anfernee Simons 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351851/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2025–2026)===
On July 7, 2025, Simons was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Jrue Holiday]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2025 |title=Celtics Complete Trades with Portland and Atlanta {{!}} Boston Celtics |url=https://celtics.com/news/070725-celtics-complete-trades-with-portland-and-atlanta |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=celtics.com |language=en}}</ref> On January 15, 2026, Simons recorded 39 points (including seven three-pointers), four rebounds, and four assists in a 119–114 victory over the [[2025–26 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics' Anfernee Simons: Explodes for 39 points off bench|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-anfernee-simons-explodes-for-39-points-off-bench/|access-date=March 5, 2026|website=CBS Sports|language=en}}</ref> He performed primarily in a reserve role for Boston during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 14.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.4 assists across 49 appearances for the team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anfernee Simons 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351851/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2026)===
On February 5, 2026, Simons and a 2026 second-round pick were traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Nikola Vučević]] and a 2027 second-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE ANFERNEE SIMONS AND SECOND-ROUND PICK|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-anfernee-simons-and-second-round-pick|access-date=February 5, 2026|website=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}}</ref> Simons made six appearances (five starts) for Chicago during the remainder of the season, averaging 15.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 3.0 assists.

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2026–present) ===
On July 6, 2026, Simons signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Sixers ink Anfernee Simons to reported 2-year deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/anfernee-simons-sixers-free-agency-2026 |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Simons was given the name Anfernee due to his parents, Charles and Tameka, being fans of the [[Orlando Magic]] and naming him after former player [[Penny Hardaway|Anfernee "Penny" Hardaway]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/2018/03/anfernee-simons-nba-draft-who-mock-highlights/|title=Anfernee Simons Is the NBA Draft's Man of Mystery|first=Jonathan|last=Adams|date=March 22, 2018|website=Heavy.com|access-date=April 9, 2018|archive-date=September 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929200201/https://heavy.com/sports/2018/03/anfernee-simons-nba-draft-who-mock-highlights/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 24, 2018 |title=HS Star Anfernee Simons Decides CBB Isn't for Him, but Is He Ready for the NBA? |website=Bleacher Report |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766108-hs-star-anfernee-simons-decides-cbb-isnt-for-him-but-is-he-ready-for-the-nba |access-date=May 4, 2023 |archive-date=March 23, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323190757/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766108-hs-star-anfernee-simons-decides-cbb-isnt-for-him-but-is-he-ready-for-the-nba |url-status=live }}</ref> Hardaway coached Simons during a Team USA Basketball training camp.<ref name=Kentucky/>
